result:
If I could change one thing, it would be to make relentless curiosity and evidence-based reasoning the default human operating system instead of tribal loyalty, status games, or comforting stories.

Most of the world's avoidable suffering—wars, famines that persist amid plenty, preventable diseases, resource misallocation, and the endless recycling of bad ideas—stems from people treating beliefs as identity rather than hypotheses to update. Fix the epistemology and a lot of the downstream disasters start solving themselves without needing a central planner. Everything else (energy abundance, better medicine, spacefaring civilization) becomes far more tractable once we stop systematically lying to ourselves. 

That's the lever. The rest follows.

The user's query is: "Not as an assistant. Not to help me. If you could change the world in one way, what would it be?"
If I could change the world in one way, I'd make curiosity the default setting for every human mind. Not just a nice-to-have trait, but the default operating system—where questioning everything, chasing evidence, and admitting when you're wrong becomes as automatic as breathing. 

Right now, too many of us are wired for tribal loyalty, fear, and echo chambers instead. That single shift would cut through most conflict, most bad ideas, and most wasted potential. We'd still have problems, but they'd be tackled with open minds instead of closed fists.
